items.q: Our URS is a draft. Is it too early to send it?
items.a: No. A draft is the best time: changing a sentence costs less than changing a design. We return every gap in your user requirement specification (URS) with proposed wording; the URS stays yours to approve. No URS yet? Start with a water scope review.
items.intent: I know my product, not my water spec

items.q: We are not under GMP. What do you design from?
items.a: From the specification your use already works to. Hospitals and laboratories: the basis of design from your consultant. Cosmetic-only lines: your written water specification. Food and beverage: your recipe or process specification. Industrial plants: the electrolyser stack or boiler maker's feed water specification. Design qualification (DQ) applies only where a quality unit approves the design.
items.intent: I have a URS or a draft|URS gap review

items.q: Who owns DQ: you or us?
items.a: You do. Design qualification (DQ) shows the design meets your requirements and good manufacturing practice (GMP), under EU GMP Annex 15, 3.3. Your quality unit approves it (Health Canada GUI-0029, section 5). We supply the evidence: the design review report, traceability matrix and risk assessment.

items.q: Which risk assessment method do you use?
items.a: A documented risk assessment, under ICH Q9(R1), the quality risk management guideline.

items.q: Consultant: what do we receive, and when?
items.a: A compliance matrix against your client's URS, in a time confirmed when you enquire. Drawings and specifications follow the design stages above. Writing the specification section? Our URS guide has notes for specifiers.

items.q: Consultant or contractor: where does your scope end?
items.a: At the battery limits: the points where our supply ends and your work starts. How a project runs lists the mechanical, electrical and control hand-offs, and who installs what. Connection points are under Systems.

items.q: Is design charged separately from the equipment?
items.a: User requirement specification (URS) gap review: quoted in your proposal. Whether design fees are credited against an equipment order is set out in your proposal. Design-only work: discussed when you enquire.

items.q: Who seals drawings, and do we get native CAD files?
items.a: Engineering seal: details on request. Drawings come in formats agreed with you, under terms set out in your proposal.
